rot.philidor.curiosidades.philidor: The French chess player and composer François-André Danican Philidor published the analysis of this position in 1777: with Black to move, the rook is lost wherever it goes.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: this is Philidor's position. The rook on b7, glued to the black king, is protected by it and blocks your queen's checks along the b-file.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.e2: If it were White to move, the rook would not fall at once. Black is to move, and every move makes things worse: that is zugzwang. The black king has only c8; the other moves are rook moves.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.e3: On b6, c7, d7, b5 or b4, the rook is captured. On a7, it takes its own king's flight square, and the queen mates on d8. The rook can only run far away.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.l1: The rook runs to b1, far from your king. A check on the b-file would attack it, but the rook would capture the queen.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.l2: Your queen checks on d8, and the black king has only a7. The check on e5 is just as good.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.l3: Forced: the king goes to a7.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.l4: Another check, now on d4. The target is h7: from there, the queen checks along the seventh rank and attacks b1 along the diagonal.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.l5: The king goes to the corner, a8. On b8, the same check on h8 would follow.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.l6: Your queen checks on h8, along the eighth rank, and arrives next to h7.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.l7: The king goes back to a7. If the rook blocked the check on b8, the queen would mate on a1.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.l8: Check on h7, along the seventh rank, and the queen attacks b1 along the diagonal: a fork, king and rook at the same time.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.l9: The king steps out of check, and the rook is left undefended. Blocking on b7 does not help either: the queen captures with mate.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex1.l10: Your queen captures the rook. With the rook won, queen against lone king is left, a mate you already know.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: Philidor's position again, with Black to move. What if the rook runs along the seventh rank instead of the b-file?
rot.philidor.ideia.ex2.l1: The rook goes to h7, far from your king, this time in the other direction.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex2.l2: Your queen checks on e5. The target now is b1: from there, the queen checks along the b-file and attacks h7 along the same diagonal as before.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex2.l3: The king goes to the corner, a8. On a7, the same check on a1 would follow.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex2.l4: Your queen checks on a1, along the a-file, and the black king can only go to b8.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex2.l5: The king goes to b8. Blocking with the rook on a7 would be worse: the queen would mate on h8.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex2.l6: Check on b1, along the b-file, and the queen attacks h7 along the diagonal: the same fork, from the other end.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex2.l7: The king steps out of check, and the rook is left undefended. Blocking on b7 does not help either: the queen captures with mate.
rot.philidor.ideia.ex2.l8: The rook is won. Far from its king, the rook is undefended, and the checks bring the queen to the fork square.
rot.philidor.demos.cravada.1: Attack demonstration: Black moved the king to c8, and the rook stayed on b7, on the king's diagonal. Look for the move that ties it down there.
rot.philidor.demos.cravada.2: Without check, your queen goes to a6 and pins the rook: if it leaves b7, the black king is in check.
rot.philidor.demos.cravada.3: The king goes to d8 and breaks the pin. On b8, it would break it too, but the queen would capture the rook with mate.
rot.philidor.demos.cravada.4: Your queen captures the rook, which was left far from the black king and undefended. The rook is won.
rot.philidor.demos.garfo.1: Attack demonstration: the rook went to e7, close by, but away from the black king, which no longer protects it. Look for the check that also attacks the rook.
rot.philidor.demos.garfo.2: Check on b4, along the b-file, and the queen attacks e7 along the diagonal: a fork. On d8, the check would also attack the rook.
rot.philidor.demos.garfo.3: The king steps out of check, and the rook is left undefended.
rot.philidor.demos.garfo.4: Your queen captures the rook. One check was enough.
rot.philidor.demos.escada.1: Attack demonstration: the rook is far from the black king and undefended. The target is e4, the fork square; the queen gets there with check in two moves.
rot.philidor.demos.escada.2: Check on e8, along the eighth rank, and the black king has only h7. The check on h3 also wins the rook, in the same number of moves.
rot.philidor.demos.escada.3: Forced: the king goes to h7, its only square. Now e4 lies on the king's diagonal.
rot.philidor.demos.escada.4: Check on e4, along the diagonal to h7, and the queen attacks b7 along the other diagonal: the fork.
rot.philidor.demos.escada.5: The king steps out of check, and the rook is left undefended. On h8 or h6 it would be the same.
rot.philidor.demos.escada.6: Your queen captures the rook. The first check did not attack the rook: it brought the queen to the fork square.
rot.philidor.pratica.fins.afogado: Stalemate: a draw. Before a move without check, make sure the black king still has a square.
rot.philidor.pratica.fins.repeticao: The position was repeated three times: a draw. Each check should bring the queen closer to the fork square.
rot.philidor.pratica.fins.limite: The move limit ran out before the rook fell. Look for the check that also attacks the rook, or the one that brings the queen to it.
rot.philidor.pratica.fins.insuficiente: Only the kings are left: a draw. Capture the rook only when the black king cannot capture the queen afterwards.
rot.philidor.pratica.garfo.err.captura: On that square, the queen is within reach of the rook or the black king and is captured.
rot.philidor.pratica.garfo.err.espeto: The rook gives check, the white king moves, and the rook captures the queen, which was on the same line, behind it.
rot.philidor.pratica.garfo.err.xeques: The rook gives checks in a row, and the white king cannot shake them off; capturing the rook may stalemate the black king. A draw.
rot.philidor.pratica.garfo.p: Attack: play White and win the rook. It has moved away from the black king and is undefended.
rot.philidor.pratica.garfo.fim: One check that also attacked the rook decided it: the rook fell, or mate came.
rot.philidor.pratica.escada.err.captura: On that square, the queen is within reach of the rook or the black king and is captured.
rot.philidor.pratica.escada.err.solta: The rook was already attacking the queen, and the king move does not save it: the rook captures the queen.
rot.philidor.pratica.escada.err.espeto: The rook gives check, the white king moves, and the rook captures the queen, which was on the same line, behind it.
rot.philidor.pratica.escada.err.xeques: The rook gives checks in a row, and the white king cannot shake them off; capturing the rook may stalemate the black king. A draw.
rot.philidor.pratica.escada.p: Attack: play White and win the rook. The checks that attack it now give the queen away: give checks in a row until the fork square.
rot.philidor.pratica.escada.fim: End of the chapter: check by check, the queen reached the fork square, and the rook fell.
